title: The background pipeline and the upload and sample routes
request: Home is where a problem becomes a solution: the user writes one sentence (or asks for any kind of model), brings data or not, and while the data is structured, cleaned and described in the background, a chat at the bottom asks a few questions about the real problem and an agent draws a solution workflow for this specific problem that follows the conversation. This package runs structuring, cleaning and analysis in the background while the user stays on Home, and reports each step live.
spec: draft/pipeline.py (structure, clean, analyse as a background job that writes events) and the routes PUT /api/drafts/{id}/data?filename= and POST /api/drafts/{id}/data/sample. Done when the sample-then-build flow test passes and make product-e2e passes upload and log-file.
plan: Write new_asset to register a data source and run() to move it through structuring, cleaning and analysing to ready or failed.
Emit a 'pipeline' event at each step and an 'analysis' event at the end, then tell the Home agent the data is ready.
Save the cleaned table as Parquet in the draft.
Add the upload route (raw body, sanitised file name, size limit) and the studied-sample route; both return at once and run the pipeline in a thread.
Report failures to the user in plain words without crashing the job.

decisions.decision: The routes return immediately and the work runs with asyncio.to_thread.
decisions.why: The user stays on Home and keeps chatting while the file is processed.

decisions.decision: The cleaned table is stored as Parquet.
decisions.why: It keeps the types cleaning established (dates, integers, booleans); a CSV would lose them on the way to the project.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/pipeline.py and the upload and studied-sample routes; each step is an event on the draft's stream.

findings.defect: A reader could see a data source marked ready with no analysis yet.
findings.scenario: The pipeline saved the asset as 'ready' in one update and the analysis, cleaning log and active asset in the next; a reader in between (the page, the Home agent, a test polling for ready) saw ready data with nothing to show. The PostgreSQL run of the draft-flow test failed on exactly that once.
findings.cause: One logical change was written as two writes.
findings.test: tests/test_draft_flow.py full-flow test, stable on files and on PostgreSQL.
findings.impact: Between the two writes, the Home page or a script polling for 'ready' found a ready table with no analysis, cleaning log or active asset, and could show an empty analysis card. On PostgreSQL the draft-flow test failed on it once, which made the suite look flaky rather than the code wrong.

findings.defect: The project upload route wrote the file under the name the caller sent, so a name such as ../x landed outside the project's data folder.
findings.scenario: While mounting the draft routes, a check for studio.data.safe_name failed: the function did not exist. The existing project upload route called it only if present, so PUT /api/projects/{id}/data?filename=../x wrote the body one folder up, into the project's own folder, and a longer chain of ../ reached further.
findings.cause: The route guarded the call with hasattr(studio_data, "safe_name") and fell back to the raw name; the sanitiser it expected had never been written, and the guard hid that.
findings.fix: safe_name now exists in studio/data.py (the last path part, safe characters only, no leading dots, at most 120 characters); the project route calls it unconditionally and answers 422 when nothing is left, and the draft upload route uses the same rule.
findings.test: tests/test_studio.py test_project_flow_over_http uploads ../evil.csv and expects the stored name evil.csv; tests/test_draft_flow.py uploads ../../tickets.csv to a draft.
findings.impact: A request with filename=../project.json would have written over the project's own record, and a deeper ../ chain could put uploaded bytes anywhere the server's user can write, outside the workspace. The server listens on loopback and needs the request token, so the caller had to be a page or script on the machine, but a mistyped or hostile name was enough.
findings.open: At this commit each route had to call the sanitiser itself, and a new route that forgot would repeat the defect. The file storage added later (9.3) refuses any key with '..' or a leading slash as a second line.

measurements.name: end-to-end flows
measurements.gate: make product-e2e passes the upload flow (the Telco CSV) and the log-file flow on a temporary server without a model.
measurements.result: Both flows passed; a web-server log was parsed at 100% and got a descriptive analysis.
measurements.against_gate: Both flows the gate names passed, the upload of the Telco CSV and the log file, and the web-server log was parsed at 100%.
limits: No model was configured, so the model's parse pattern and the chat's model path were not exercised.
The log was written by the check itself in the standard combined format, so a full parse shows the built-in reader works, not that messy real logs parse.
One public CSV and one log; a pass shows the flow completes, not that the analysis is right.
One run: the ready-without-analysis race showed up only on a later PostgreSQL run.

outcome: Done: data is prepared in the background with every step streamed to Home.
lessons: A status flag and the data it promises must be written together; a reader will land between two writes sooner or later.
risks: A long upload or parse run on the server's event loop freezes Home for every user.
A status flag written apart from the data it promises lets a reader see 'ready' with nothing to show.
A file name from the user can escape the draft's data folder ('../x') unless it is sanitised.
An oversized upload fills the disk unless the route caps its size.
A cleaned table stored as CSV loses the types cleaning established.
